featured_reviews.name: Yogita Uchil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Whenever I’m in a new city, I make it a point to explore its traditional flavors. In Mumbai, Malvani food is always on my list. Since I was staying near Malad West, I decided to try Surmai, a Malvani/Mangalorean restaurant.
We ordered quite a few dishes, and while there were some good ones, the experience was mixed overall. Unfortunately, the signature dishes were a letdown. The fish curry in the thali was bland, lacking any real flavor, and the fish itself seemed like old stock. The bangda/mackerel fry was also disappointing, with fish that tasted frozen and not fresh.
On the brighter side, the clam sukka and prawn rava fry were enjoyable and definitely stood out. The sol kadhi, however, was more about color than taste and lacked the authentic punch.
I wish the restaurant paid more attention to freshness and flavor, especially in their star dishes, because Malvani food deserves much better representation.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Hits and misses at this Mangalorean spot:

​I visited The Fisherman’s Kitchen on a Friday evening with high expectations, given the name and the positive reviews. While the atmosphere is family-friendly and the location is convenient (right below Bangur Nagar Metro with valet parking), the food was a mixed bag.
​The Standouts: The Pomfret in Banana Leaf was easily the highlight—the fish was incredibly fresh and perfectly cooked (4.5/5). Pairing the remaining gravy with Neer Dosa was the best part of the meal.
​The Letdowns: Unfortunately, the Prawns Tandoori didn't taste fresh (2.5/5), and the Crab Soup was watery with very little meat. The Kadipatta Chicken was also quite average; the chicken felt a bit tough and lacked that punchy Mangalorean flavor I was looking for.
​The Verdict:
​Ambience & Service: 3.5/5
​Alcohol Variety: 4/5
Food: 3/5
​Value for Money: 3/5
It’s a decent place for a family outing, and perhaps I caught them on an off-night, but for a seafood specialty restaurant, I expected more consistency in freshness.

featured_reviews.name: jeet sandhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Konkan Chilli Restaurant offers a delightful journey into the rich and vibrant flavors of the Konkan coast, known for its unique blend of spices and coastal ingredients. Tucked away in an unassuming corner, this restaurant might not grab attention at first glance, but once inside, you’re welcomed with a warm, homely ambiance that sets the stage for a memorable dining experience.

The menu is a reflection of authentic Konkani cuisine, with dishes that boast a perfect balance between heat and subtlety, particularly through their generous use of local spices, tamarind, and coconut. One of the standout dishes is their fish thali, which includes a fresh, perfectly cooked fish curry, tangy sol kadhi, rice, and a variety of sides that highlight the diversity of flavors on the Konkan belt. For spice lovers, the prawn masala is a must-try, offering a kick of heat that lingers pleasantly on the palate without overwhelming the delicate taste of the prawns.

Vegetarian options are equally impressive, with their jackfruit and brinjal curries being particularly noteworthy. The dishes are served with a smile, and the service is attentive without being intrusive. The staff is knowledgeable about the menu and are happy to recommend dishes to suit your taste preferences.

What truly elevates the experience at Konkan Chilli is the authenticity of the flavors, making you feel like you're savoring a home-cooked meal from the coastal regions of Maharashtra or Goa. The prices are reasonable, especially considering the quality and freshness of the ingredients. For anyone looking to explore Konkani cuisine or simply craving a hearty, flavorful meal, Konkan Chilli Restaurant is a gem worth visiting..!! ,😁🤩

featured_reviews.name: Anish Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Konkan chilly, Malad (West)

❖ My Recommendations-
• Tandoori Pomfret
• Prawn Koliwada
• Surmai tawa fry
• Prawn dum biryani

❖ Location- Malad west area got so many foodie residents so yes the location is so ideal to be honest opp to evershine mall just near link road. (4/5)

❖ Theme- Though the name has konkan in it, they don’t serve only Konkani food, they have oriental and north Indian food too in the restaurant.(4/5)

❖ Ambience- Honestly nothing much to speak about, had little odd kind of smell as soon as we enter inside might be surrounding smell of the entrance (outside their restaurant). God good number of seating in the restaurant. Walls got nice pictures of all the Indian spices giving an aromatic touch. In all interiors were ok types keeping in mind that they must be doing lot of delivery orders.(4/5)

❖ Food and Beverage- Food menu is never ending to be honest, it’s huge and I really wonder and appreciate the chef’s inside who manages such a lengthy menu from kitchen. As I am saying menu is lengthy I was surprised that each dish was available. Menu consists of Konkani food, Chinese and north Indian food. We were totally focused and pre decided that we were wanted to have Konkani food from their menu. Beverages are taken aback sit here and expected so. They have few mocktails like mojito’s which you might be able to try to keep yourself going along with delicious food, especially pineapple mojito which was excellent. Food really won my heart in konkan chilly. Each dish had its own unique flavour and taste (4.5/5)

• BOMBAY DUCK FRY- Super crispy coated bombil marinated with just little seasoning and masala tasted superb. Coated with guess rice flour and rawa to give the perfect crisp. Good part here was that bombil has tendency to be very water but here it was not.(4/5)

• SURAMAI TAW FRY- Surmai slice marinated in malvani masala with little more punch of tamarind to give a sweet and sour taste and then shallow fried on tawa. Fish was fried perfectly to be honest, was moist and flavourful. (4.5/5)

• FISH TIKKA- Chunks of fish marinated in tikka marination and cooked in tandoor to give a perfect starter. Marination of the fish and cooking time was really spot on here to be honest. Really feel a must order dish of konkan chilly.(5/5)

• TANDOORI POMFRET- Here comes Dish of the Meal. Whole medium size (Medium because we told them to bring medium) pomfret fish marinated nicely in tandoori marination and cooked to the perfection. Marination was little sweetish than normal which was really nice and fish was marinated well enough so each meat part of the fish had marination to be honest. It’s a must try dish of this restaurant, believe me you would love it to the core.(5/5)

• PRAWN KOLIWADA- Medium size prawns coated in koliwada style marination and then fried crispy enough. little squeeze of lemon wedge and yes they are ready to be nailed.(4.5/5)

❖ To sum up- A wow factor is always a mixer of interiors, location, service and food and beverage department of the restaurant. Food was amazing to be honest we nailed it really. Balancing of flavours, cooking timing was something I really liked and appreciates the chef inside who managed it very well along with your never ending menu. From this restaurant I felt location and interiors are just side hero’s as their main hero which was Food was extraordinary. I would be one of your regular guests, hope to try few other dishes from the menu and off course Chinese and north Indian cuisine next time. Thank you so much for excellent food and hospitality, All the Best.

featured_reviews.name: Tanvi Khare
featured_reviews.review_text:
This decade old iconic restaurant has made its mark in th nusy corporate area of Mindspace pleasing and satisfying the hungerpangs of people from all generations. Konkan Chilly is a restaurant serving some of the most authentic Malvani delicacies along with delicious Indian & Chinese options as well. Recently visited this place again with my pals & felt so nostalgic. The management is on point & the service is very warm thanks to its sweet lady owner who herself is present all the time even after being in business now for 10 years. Overall this is our take on @konkanchilly:

Ambience: 4/5
Service:5/5
Food: 5/5
Creativity: 5/5

Food we ordered:

1. Chicken Koliwada: To start with we ordered the must have for every Malvani cuisine lover and that is Chicken Koliwada. Small tender chunks of chicken nicely marinated in Malvani spiced marination and deep fried. Served with some fresh mint chutney. A dash of lemon and some onions is all you need to relish on this snack. Totally worth it & highly recommended.

2. Prawns Fry: Secondly we tried this delicious starter in prawns. Medium sized prawns coated in tangy spicy marination and semolina, deep fried to perfect crunchy bites. These were too good and complimented well with the schezwan dip. They also went well with the mint dip. Another must have indeed..

3. White Tandoori: On their recommendation we tried this white tandoori chicken. If you love chicken kalimiri or malai style then you are gonna absolutely love this. One of their best sellers, it’s a whole chicken marinated in creamy batter with some pepper and roasted to nice charr grilled flavor. Another stunner on table indeed..

4. Kolambi Bhaat: For the Mains we ordered this prawns rice based dish. Its extremely spicy but equally delicious, a very nice balance. The rice was tossed well in prawns coconut preparation for that perfect balance of spice and flavor. Totally nailed it.

5. Kombadi Wade Thali: Obviously who would miss an authentic thali experience when in such a place. I truly am a Kombadi wade lover and this was definitely on point. The thali consisted of Chicken Masala dry, Chicken Rassa, Kombadi Wade, Salad, Steam Rice, Papad & Solkadi. Definitely worth every penny.

6. Desserts: For desserts we hd some nice hot soft gulab jamuns which were quite fresh and some yummy caramel custard. Something we needed to balance out all the spices..

7. Beverages: For refreshments we had a Classic Virjin Mojito & a Virgin Kiwi Mojito, both of them were on point and quite refreshing to the palate..

Overall I truly enjoyed the visit & am truly glad the quality of food as well as quantity is no wehere compromised in all these years. Also the service is still on point. The ambience and décor definitely has got a massive uplift as per the recent trend with calm bluish undertone decors and some peppy music on the background. A special mention to the owner who inspite of all odds makes it a point to personally check with customers for feedback whenever shes around. We definitely need such service. Totally recommended.

Happy Fooding 🙂

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
This visit to Kokan Katta turned out to be extremely disappointing and uncomfortable, and honestly, it was not an experience I would recommend to anyone. We visited this place as a group of three friends (all men), and right from the beginning, we felt that we were treated differently compared to families and couples present in the restaurant. We were not loud, not misbehaving, and not creating any disturbance — yet there was a visible change in attitude from the staff, as if they had already assumed something just because we were three guys.

The service itself was careless. One of the items we ordered was butter garlic naan, which arrived burnt with an unpleasant, bitter garlic taste. When I politely asked for a replacement, instead of correcting the mistake properly, the staff simply brought plain naan, without butter or garlic, and without even informing us. There was no apology, no explanation, and no attempt to actually fix the issue. This kind of response shows a lack of basic customer courtesy.

Things got worse as the night progressed. Around 11:45 pm, the staff suddenly started telling us that we need to leave and that they would not serve us anymore. What made this even more frustrating was that earlier we were clearly told that last order would be taken at 12:00 am. Despite this, we were pushed to leave early. At the same time, we could clearly see families and couples still seated comfortably, being served without any urgency or pressure. This selective behaviour felt unfair and discriminatory.

The entire situation left us feeling unwelcome and embarrassed, especially when we had travelled all the way from Goregaon East to Malad West, based purely on a friend’s recommendation, just to try this place. Sadly, the effort was completely wasted. Even the food quality was below average. The taste was disappointing and, frankly, quite bad. None of the dishes we tried stood out positively — instead, they added to the frustration of the overall experience.

A restaurant that labels itself as a “family restaurant and bar” should know how to treat all customers equally, regardless of whether they are families, couples, or a group of friends. Respect and consistency should not change based on the type of guests at the table.

Overall, this visit left a very poor impression — bad food, careless service, and uncomfortable behaviour from the staff. I will not be visiting again, and I would not recommend this place to anyone, especially groups of friends. One star is being given only because zero is not an option.

Just had a fantastic meal at Kokan Katta in Malad, and I gotta say, it was a true taste of Konkan! For all my seafood lovers out there, this place is a must-try.

Here's what I devoured (and absolutely recommend)

Khekda Thali : This crab thali was the star of the show! The khekda curry was bursting with flavor, and the accompaniments like solkadi and rice were perfect.

Spl Chicken Thali : Even my non-seafood loving friend was impressed with this chicken thali. The chicken was cooked perfectly, and the gravy was delicious.

Bombil Fry: Crispy on the outside and flaky on the inside, these Bombay Duck fries were simply divine.

Prawns Koliwada : A Konkan classic done right! The prawns were juicy and flavorful, with a hint of spice.

Surmai Tawa Fry: This kingfish fry was cooked to perfection. The fish was fresh and flaky, and the masala was incredibly flavorful.

Overall, Kokan Katta is a hidden gem in Malad. The food is delicious, the service is friendly, and the prices are reasonable. I left feeling happy, satisfied, and already planning my next visit!

Pro Tip: Make sure you try their Solkadi, it's the perfect way to cool down your palate after all that delicious seafood!

featured_reviews.name: Anmol Menon
featured_reviews.review_text:
Booked on District Zomato: 35% discount.

We were escorted by the hostess in and she just kind of disappeared half way through the process.

We were seated at a table, that was not set, the table top was sticky. We were then requested to get up while they cleaned the table.

I absolutely hate scanned menu. It just screams, i don't care whether you order or not. This is a bar, drink up and leave.

Price were overly inflated considering Zomato district discount. 500 for a manchow soup to give you an idea.

We had to keep searching for a steward to take our order.

Food:

Manchow soup: was decent. (3/5)

Appetizers:

Smoked salmon sushi:
the sushi roll was good. What was a downer was the quality of the wasabi. It seemed super diluted missing the kick it should have and had a sweet after taste. The pickled ginger was also very underwhelming and had a bitter after taste. The soy sauce didn't taste like kikkoman. 4 pieces (3/5)

Smoked butter chicken ghujiya:
A little gimmicky. Wasn't shaped like a ghujiya. More like a parcel. Inside was minced meat, some mozzarella cheese. Came with a side of very basic makhani gravy which passed of as a sauce, a little bit of onion salad. Was passable (3/5)  (4 pieces)

Bangkok style chilli chicken:

It was a take on salt and pepper dried chilli chicken. The chicken itself was delicious. There was way too many aromatics (chunks of lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves) vegetables, the onions were slightly underdone, missing smokiness and complexity required. But overall really nice.  (3/5)

Wanted to order lamb seekh. It was unavailable.

Mains:

Chicken Bulgogi Pizza: the crust was nice and crisp. However The smoky flavour of Bulgogi was missing from the meat and the mushrooms. Not quite sure why there was corn in my pizza though. There was just a hint of gochujang sauce. It seemed like a basic bbq chicken pizza. Taste was decent. It needs to be more Korean forward. (3/5)

Nasi Goreng Chicken:
Good portion size. Rice was well cooked. Got 1 skewer of chicken satay which was missing seasoning. Peanut sauce quantity was very less. (2 tsp) at most. The infamous corn made another appearance. Was missing more punch from sambal and no evidence of sweet soy sauce. It was a good spicy fried rice. Wouldn't call it nasi Goreng. (3/5)

Spaghetti In White Sauce:
Well cooked, creamy, my parents liked it. Good portion size. (4/5)

Drinks:

Diet coke was not available.

Pasion fruit iced tea was good but was not having the passion fruit flavour.

Order a couple of fresh lime sodas which were as expected, good.

Service: was average. Small details which were annoying.

Table not set/ clean before seating guests

The soup was just directly placed in our used appetizers plates.

Ambience: straight out of a squid game set. But nice, sleek. A little too dark for my liking. I couldn't see what I was eating. The led lamp on the table was just super dim.

The bill for 5 people came up to 8.5 k. After discount was around 5.5k. This review would have been vastly different if the bill had been. 8.5k.

It was decent but I don't think I'll be visiting again. Everything ain't hunky dory. 🫡

customer_updates.text:
I’ve tried Flavours of China only once or twice, but based on my experience, it’s a decent spot in Malad West for satisfying Indo-Chinese cravings without spending too much.

Restaurant Review for Flavours of China

Flavours of China offers a delightful dining experience that lives up to its name. The restaurant's vibrant ambiance and comfortable seating make it a perfect spot if you want to experience desi chinese.

The dishes served were flavorful and well-presented. The Foc Lollypop Masala Dry was a standout, offering a perfect balance of spice and texture. It was served in green chatney which was unique to this restaurant. The Chicken Oriental Noodles were another highlight, with a rich, aromatic flavor containing flat noodles and exotic Veges with a kick of spiciness to it. The mocktails , including the Black Tart and Oceanic Orange, were refreshing and rounded off the meal beautifully.

The service was prompt and courteous, and the staff ensured a smooth dining experience. The pricing, considering the portion sizes and quality, was reasonable and value for money.

Overall, Flavours of China is a must-visit for Desi Chinese cuisine lovers seeking a comfortable dining experience. Recommended for its food and service.

featured_reviews.name: Shaikh Khalid Sarfaraz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flavours of China is located on the main Malad Link Road and is is beside the famous Greens Veg restaurant hence easy to locate. Apart from this they have other outlets at Lalbaug, Parel, Dadar, Prabhadevi, Matunga, Bandra & Borivali.

The restaurant is decent in size with ground plus basement seating available. They have perfectly utilised every part of the property as the seatings are nicely arranged. The ambiance again looks great and have a nice feel of a small China theme as the walls have words written and Chinese lantern on the ceiling looks beautiful.

They specialise in Chinese and Thai food. The options available are great for both vegetarians and non vegetarians. Alao they have acquired Icecreaft ice creams hence you get great options in desserts as well. Prices are not too high and th quantity served is huge. Apart from this they also serve combos which indeed is super pocket friendly.

I went here for a weekday dinner and the place got packed around 9PM. The kitchen service was smooth and dishes came on time. The table service by Staff Rahan was perfect as he was attentive. Special mention to Manager Ganesh as honestly he was among the few managers that I came accross who were very professional and polite plus fully committed to their job. He knew the menu well and he suggested grest options for us. And he single handedly was taking care of all the tables.

What We Had -
APPETIZERS~
Malaysian Chicken -
Sliced chicken done in peanut based creamy sauce tasted delicious. Loved the juiciness of the chicken and the peanut sauce had a hint of chilli in it hence you don't feel too much of peanuts in this.

Chicken Lollypop Schezwan Dry -
Huge lollypops done in schezwan sauce tasted outstanding. The size of the lollypops and the meat on it was marvellous. The sauce again had load of garlic in it still not to overpowering. A must try for lollypop lovers.

MAINS~
Chicken Oriental Noodles -
Flat noodles with exotic veggies, chicken and egg tasted good. Didn't had too much of spices  but taste wise it wasn't bland and had nice taste due to the multiple ingredients in it.

Chicken Five Spice Fried Rice -
Aromatic five spice done in fried rice with chicken and veggies tasted great. Loved the taste of the five spice as it doesn't taste like the normal fried rice.

DESSERTS~
Loconuts Ice Cream Roll -
Chocolate ice cream, almonds, brownie and chocolate sauce tasted heavenly. A great end to a perfect meal.

MOCKTAILS~
Oceanic Orange.
Grey Mango.
Both the drinks were nicely made with perfect ratio of syrup and soda hence perfect.

So the meal at Flavours of China was excellent from start to end as the food taste excellent, the service is great and the ambiance is nice. Hence this place should not be missed.
